plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Great ruffled blooms open from plump buds. Their silky petals hold a sweet, rosy fragrance. Gardeners treasure them for flowers the size of saucers, which sway over glossy, deeply cut leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, typically May to early June in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Temperate gardens across North America and Europe, native to China, Mongolia and Siberia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and flower for more than 50 years in the same spot. Many gardeners are surprised to find they dislike being moved.

plants.name: Rosa banksiae
plants.description: A vigorous, thornless climbing rose that can drape whole walls and porches in cascading clusters of tiny, softly scented blossoms. In full flower it looks like a waterfall of butter-yellow or snowy white.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, generally April to May in mild climates
plants.location: Native to China, widely grown in the southern United States and Mediterranean-climate gardens
plants.funFact: A Lady Banks' rose planted in Tombstone, Arizona, in the 1880s is often described as the largest rose bush in the world. It spreads over a vast arbor.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: Dense, cone-shaped clusters of tiny, star-shaped flowers perfume the air with one of spring's most beloved scents. The shrubs light up cool-climate gardens and old farmhouse hedgerows.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring, usually May in cool temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens in northern Europe, the northern United States and Canada, native to the Balkans
plants.funFact: Lilac is a member of the olive family. Its flowers are edible and have a floral, slightly lemony flavor.
